datasets.name: lamm-mit/CategoryTheoryDesign gh_scripts (code of Marom, Tibbits, Zardini & Buehler 2026, JMPS 106780)
datasets.role: independent reference implementation of the strain-projection and Timoshenko steps; file hashes recorded by analysis.py

hypothesis: The Lean definitions shearStrain and axialStrain (ThompsonLaws/Hygromorphs.lean) and the strain projection published with Marom et al. (2026) (T_tis.py and T_stack.py, run unmodified) compute the same functions: for every draw, the strip-axis strain and the in-plane shear strain of each layer, and the through-thickness and shear mismatches, agree within the rounding bound; and for antisymmetric fibre angles with equal layers the published pipeline gives zero axial mismatch and a shear mismatch (epsL - epsT) sin 2 phi, as shearStrain_mismatch and axialStrain_mismatch state.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered (supported). In every one of the 8 configurations and the antisymmetric sets, for all draws, eps_strip_1, eps_strip_2, delta_12_1, delta_12_2, delta_eps_thk and delta_eps_12 from the published scripts equal the Lean-defined values within the rounding bound; in the antisymmetric sets |delta_eps_thk| <= 1e-6 and |delta_eps_12 - (epsL - epsT) sin 2 phi| <= 1e-6; and the controls detect all faults relevant to this claim (L1, L2, L3, M1, M2, M4). Rounding-aware bound: the published scripts serialize every bundle value with {:.6f} (angles and thicknesses with {:.4f}), so the inputs above are on grids that survive serialization exactly and the only expected discrepancy is output rounding. Strain-like quantities (eps_strip_i, delta_12_i) must agree within 5e-7 + 1e-12; mismatches (delta_eps_thk, delta_eps_12) within 1e-6 + 1e-12; kappa within |C_geom| * 1e-6 + 5e-7 + 1e-12. Sampling (fixed before running; seed 20261101, numpy default_rng): per configuration N = 1000 draws. chi or alpha on a 1e-4 grid in [-0.2, 0.3] (per layer, L and T), humidity RH_ref in 0..50 % and RH in 50..100 % (integers) or T_ref in 0..50 and T_cur in 50..150 C (integers), theta_1 and theta_2 on a 0.01 degree grid in [-90, 90], h_1 and h_2 on a 1e-4 cm grid in [0.02, 0.2], E_1 and E_2 log-uniform in [100, 20000] rounded to integers, L = 8, W = 1.2, with |chi_L - chi_T| >= 0.005 in each layer. Configurations: stimulus (hygro, thermal) x branch (Nat: F_fib..S_elem; Art: F_fil..S_print) x response (beta_bend, beta_twist) = 8. Plus an antisymmetric set of 500 draws per branch with theta_2 = -theta_1, equal layer materials and beta_twist and beta_bend each. Controls (fault injection, pre-registered): five faults are injected one at a time into the Lean-side expressions (L1 sin(2 phi) -> sin(phi) in shearStrain; L2 cos^2/sin^2 swapped in axialStrain; L3 factor 1/2 dropped from shearStrain; L4 6(1+m)^2 -> 3(1+m)^2 in timoshenkoCoefficient; L5 (1+m n) -> (1+m/n) in timoshenkoCoefficient) and four into the vendored scripts (M1 sin(2.0*r1) -> sin(r1) in T_tis; M2 radians() dropped from theta_2 in T_tis; M3 (1.0+m*n) -> (1.0+m/n) in S_elem; M4 d12_1 - d12_2 -> d12_1 + d12_2 in beta_twist). Every fault relevant to a claim must trip the rounding-aware bound in at least 90 % of the draws of every configuration it affects, otherwise the harness cannot see transcription errors and the verdict is inconclusive (reason other).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered (refuted). Any draw in an unmutated configuration exceeds the bound for any of the quantities above. That is a discrepancy between the Lean definitions and the published code (a sign, angle-convention, or transcription error on one side); it is reported with the first failing inputs and is not explained away. If the controls fail to detect a relevant fault, the verdict is 'inconclusive' with reason 'other'.
interpretation: A computational consistency check, not a test of the claim in organisms. The Lean proofs establish the identities; this checks that the formalized definitions are the functions the authors implemented (angle in radians vs degrees, ordering of layers, sign of the shear, which layer carries eps_L). The published code is run verbatim by exec-ing the Grasshopper scripts with their input ports as globals; nothing is edited. The Lean definitions are read from the Lean source file by a small term parser, not retyped. It shows the formalization and the code agree; it does not show either matches pine cones, and the paper's measured-vs-predicted actuator results are not reproduced (the repository has videos and figures but no tables).

test_contract.expected_observation: For random inputs, every output the published pipeline shares with our Lean definitions agrees within the stated output-rounding bound.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: At least one input in an unmutated configuration where the published code and the Lean-defined function differ by more than the rounding bound.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: None: the inputs are random draws from the stated grid; the reference is the published code at a pinned commit, independent of our Lean file.
test_contract.inference_method: Exhaustive comparison over all draws against the rounding-aware bound; fault-injection controls must trip the same comparison.

method: Seed 20261101. Each of 8 configurations (stimulus x Nat/Art branch x beta_bend/beta_twist) got 1000 random draws, plus 500 antisymmetric draws per branch and response (10000 draws in all). For each draw the published Grasshopper components in vendor/ (commit fa8100bad) were exec'd unmodified in the wiring of gh_scripts/README.md, and the same inputs were evaluated with shearStrain, axialStrain, timoshenkoCoefficient and bilayerCurvature parsed from ThompsonLaws/Hygromorphs.lean by lean_eval.py. Differences were divided by the pre-registered rounding bound. The equilibrium equations of bilayerCurvature_ofEquilibrium were solved as a 2x2 linear system. Nine faults were injected one at a time as controls.

measured.unit: max |published - Lean| / rounding bound over all draws (<= 1 passes)
measured.uncertainty: deterministic given the seed; no sampling error is claimed

caveats: Output rounding is the only discrepancy permitted: the published scripts serialize bundle values with six decimals, so the comparison uses the pre-registered rounding-aware bound rather than machine precision. Agreement within that bound does not exclude differences smaller than 1e-6.

The degrees-to-radians conversion of the fibre angle is done by this harness, not by Lean: the published code takes degrees and the Lean definitions take radians. The control M2 (radians dropped from one angle) shows the harness would see a mismatch of that kind inside the published code, but a wrong conversion in the harness itself would show as a failure of every draw.

S_elem.py and S_print.py recompute the through-thickness and shear mismatches from the tissue-stage values themselves, so the final curvature does not depend on the beta reducer's output; the reducer only selects which one is active. The published pipeline is compositional in its interfaces but the mismatch is derived twice.
The inputs cover ranges (thermal strains up to 4500 %) far beyond physical ones because the identities are algebraic and domain-independent; this checks the functions, not any material.

The paper's measured-vs-predicted actuator results are not reproduced: the repository ships videos and figures, no measurement tables, and the PA612-CF and PLA material panels are not in the repository.
Computational data only: it shows the Lean definitions and the published implementation agree, not that organisms follow the claim.
